the market fell sharply shortly after the decision, with a large drawdown
the alternative of selling 100% and re-entering after a 10% drop or vol rollover returned -16.46%, worse than the action taken

autopsy.failed_assumption: that a moderate VIX (15-20) with a positive 3- and 6-month trend and a recent small drawdown indicated a bullish regime that would persist over the next 63 days, when in fact the market was about to enter a sharp correction.
autopsy.proposed_mechanism: A systematic tendency to over-weight recent positive medium-term momentum (3m and 6m returns) and under-weight the signal from a rising short-term volatility ratio (vol_ratio_20_60 > 1.3) when VIX is in the moderate 15-20 bucket. In such states, the market is often at a fragile inflection point: the short-term vol spike is a leading warning, but the recent trend makes the model overconfident, leading to a leveraged buy that amplifies losses when the correction hits. This is repeatable because the same combination of moderate VIX, positive trend, and rising short-term vol recurs in late-cycle bull markets.
expected_affected_states: moderate VIX (15-20) with rising short-term vol and positive 3-month momentum
late-cycle bull markets where short-term vol is picking up but trend is still positive
expected_unaffected_states: low VIX (<15) with stable vol ratio (vol_ratio_20_60 < 1.2) and positive trend
high VIX (>25) where the model is already cautious
autopsy.falsifier: If in the affected states (moderate VIX, rising vol ratio, positive trend) the same action swap (buy_25 vs sell_100) does not show a systematic negative excess return over many episodes, or if the same swap shows a similar negative edge in the unaffected states (low VIX, stable vol), then the mechanism is refuted.
autopsy.alternative_explanation: The loss was simply due to an unpredictable market crash (e.g., COVID-19 onset) that no conditioning on VIX or vol ratio could have anticipated; the model was just unlucky.
